timing_issues: Arithmetic verified. CH1 = 1+1+1+1 = 4.0; CH2 = 1+1+1+1.5+1.5+1.5+1 = 8.5; CH3 = 1+1.5 = 2.5; total 15.0 across 13 slides, all in 0.5 steps. Checkpoints 4.0 / 12.5 / 15.0 are correct. The 20-minute stretch plan sums to +5.0 correctly.

The talk is realistic overall. Speaker points total 1,431 words, about 95 words per minute on average (11.9 min at 120 wpm). That leaves roughly 3 minutes of slack for 3 handovers and chart pauses, but only if presenters stick to the points. The suggested split is uneven (4.0 / 3.0 / 5.5 / 2.5 min), and the 5.5-minute block (S8-S11) is the heaviest.

The heaviest slides per minute are S7 (119 words), S4 (117), S1 (107), S11 (106), S3 (105) and S12 (105). The lightest relative to on-slide text are S9 (63 words per min for about 165 on-slide words) and S13 (78).

Numbers read aloud break the outline's own cap of about 5 per minute (counted from digit tokens, so years and dates are included). S4 has 18, S7 has 16, S6 has 10 and S8 has 11 in 1.5 min (7.3 per min). S1, S2, S5 and S11 have 6 each.
S10 needs about 8 seconds per variable for 11 variables with a table of about 225 words. This works only with the three-block reveal and read-aloud limited to the block headlines.

S2 plus S5 (2.0 min) must carry two theory diagrams and two before/during/after strips with no slack. The text fallback keeps the minutes unchanged, so the timing risk does not grow if the graphs are rejected.
